subject: business-studies
topicDisplay: Analysing The Strategic Position Of A Business
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The payback period method of investment appraisal measures:
options: The present value of future cash flows
The percentage return per year on the investment
The time taken for an investment to recover its initial cost
The total profit an investment will generate
questions.explain: Payback measures how long it takes for net cash inflows to repay the initial outlay.

questions.q: According to Ansoff's matrix, the strategy of launching a new product into a new market is:
options: Market penetration, the lowest risk
Diversification, the highest risk
Product development, a moderate risk
Market development, a moderate risk
questions.explain: Diversification means new product plus new market and is the riskiest quadrant of Ansoff's matrix.

questions.q: Managing risk through a risk assessment typically involves identifying hazards and then:
options: Transferring every risk to employees
Assessing the likelihood and impact of each risk and planning mitigation
Eliminating all risk so that none remains
Ignoring low-probability events entirely
questions.explain: Risk management evaluates each risk's probability and impact and then decides how to reduce, transfer or accept it.

questions.q: A decision has two outcomes: a 0.6 chance of £100,000 and a 0.4 chance of £50,000. Its expected value is:
Monetary policy is mainly concerned with controlling:
options: Interest rates and the money supply
Government spending levels
Income tax rates
Employment law
questions.explain: Monetary policy, typically run by the central bank, manages interest rates and the money supply.

questions.q: Scenario planning is mainly used to help a business:
options: Calculate the exact break-even output
Set fixed annual sales targets with certainty
Prepare for a range of possible future situations and uncertainties
Record last year's financial results accurately
questions.explain: Scenario planning explores several plausible futures so the firm can prepare responses to uncertain conditions.

questions.q: Average rate of return (ARR) is expressed as:
options: Average annual profit as a percentage of the initial investment
The number of years to recoup the investment
The discounted value of future cash flows
Total cash inflow minus total outflow
questions.explain: ARR = (average annual profit ÷ initial investment) × 100, shown as a percentage.

questions.q: Which statement best captures the difference between strategy and tactics?
options: Strategy is short-term and reactive; tactics are long-term and planned
Strategy and tactics are interchangeable terms for the same plans
Tactics are decided by senior managers; strategy is decided by junior staff
Strategy sets long-term direction to achieve overall objectives; tactics are the shorter-term actions used to implement it
questions.explain: Strategy is the long-term plan for achieving objectives, while tactics are the day-to-day or short-term actions that carry the strategy out.

questions.q: Corporate social responsibility (CSR) refers to a firm's:
options: Requirement to avoid all taxation
Voluntary commitment to act ethically towards society and the environment
Legal duty to maximise shareholder profit only
Obligation to pay the lowest possible wages
questions.explain: CSR is a firm's voluntary responsibility to consider its impact on society, stakeholders and the environment.

questions.q: Buyer (customer) bargaining power in Porter's model tends to be highest when:
options: There are few buyers each purchasing large volumes and products are undifferentiated
There are many small buyers and products are highly differentiated
Switching costs for buyers are extremely high
The product is essential and has no alternatives
questions.explain: A small number of large buyers facing standardised products can demand lower prices, giving them strong bargaining power.

questions.q: In a decision tree, the expected value of an outcome is calculated as:
options: Probability multiplied by the outcome value, summed across outcomes
The highest possible payoff
The cost of the decision divided by its probability
The sum of all outcome values
questions.explain: Expected value = Σ(probability × outcome value) for each branch's possible results.

questions.q: A key limitation of using decision trees is that:
options: The probabilities used are often estimates that may be inaccurate
They cannot show different options at once
They ignore the cost of each decision
They can only be used for HR decisions
questions.explain: Decision trees rely on estimated probabilities and values, which may be subjective or wrong.

questions.q: Outsourcing is best defined as:
options: Relocating part of a firm's own operations to another country
Paying an external provider to carry out activities previously done in-house
Merging with a foreign competitor
Buying out a supplier to control it directly
questions.explain: Outsourcing means contracting an outside organisation to perform tasks the business used to do itself.

questions.q: A limitation of relying heavily on data for decision-making is that:
options: Past data may not reliably predict future conditions
Data can never be quantified
It removes all need for managerial judgement
Data is always completely objective and certain
questions.explain: Historical data may not hold in a changing environment, so it cannot replace managerial judgement.

questions.q: Retrenchment as a strategy involves:
options: Aggressive expansion into new markets
Reducing the scale of operations, e.g. closing divisions or cutting costs
Diversifying into unrelated products
Acquiring a major competitor
questions.explain: Retrenchment is a deliberate cutting-back of the firm's scale, often to restore profitability or focus.

questions.q: Sustainability in a business context most directly concerns:
options: Maximising short-term profit at any cost
Reducing the number of employees
Avoiding all forms of taxation
Meeting present needs without compromising future generations
questions.explain: Sustainability means meeting present needs without harming the ability of future generations to meet theirs.

questions.q: Net present value (NPV) appraisal is superior to payback because it:
options: Ignores the timing of cash flows
Accounts for the time value of money by discounting future cash flows
Requires no estimate of future cash flows
Is always quicker to calculate
questions.explain: NPV discounts future cash flows to present value, recognising that money now is worth more than later.

questions.q: During the boom phase of the economic cycle, a business is most likely to experience:
options: Sharply falling output
Rising demand and pressure on capacity
Falling demand and rising spare capacity
Deflation and high unemployment
questions.explain: In a boom, high demand and economic growth put pressure on a firm's capacity and resources.

questions.q: Consumer protection legislation primarily aims to:
options: Set the level of corporation tax
Prevent firms from merging
Limit the wages firms can pay
Protect customers from being misled or sold unsafe goods
questions.explain: Consumer law protects buyers, requiring goods to be safe, as described and fit for purpose.

questions.q: A fall in a country's exchange rate (a weaker currency) tends to:
options: Have no effect on trade
Make exports more price-competitive and imports more expensive
Reduce the cost of imported raw materials
Make imports cheaper and exports dearer
questions.explain: A weaker currency lowers the foreign price of exports (more competitive) and raises import prices.

questions.q: In Charles Handy's classification, a 'power culture' is one in which:
options: Individuals work as autonomous experts with little hierarchy
Control radiates from a central figure or small group with few rules
Authority is spread evenly across self-managing teams
Roles and procedures are rigidly defined by bureaucracy
questions.explain: A power culture centres control on a dominant individual or core group, with decisions made centrally and few formal rules.

questions.q: Offshoring differs from outsourcing because offshoring specifically means:
options: Using a third party in the same country
Selling a subsidiary to a foreign buyer
Importing finished goods from abroad
Relocating a business activity to another country (whether kept in-house or not)
questions.explain: Offshoring is relocating an activity abroad; it can be done in-house and is therefore distinct from outsourcing.

questions.q: Which of Porter's five forces is increased when there are many alternative substitute products available?
options: Bargaining power of suppliers
Barriers to exit
The threat of substitutes
Bargaining power of buyers
questions.explain: A wide range of substitutes raises the threat-of-substitutes force, limiting the prices a firm can charge.

questions.q: In a competitive (fragmented) market with many similar firms, competitive rivalry is usually:
options: Low, allowing high prices
Determined only by suppliers
High, putting downward pressure on prices
Eliminated entirely
questions.explain: Many similar competitors intensify rivalry, typically driving prices and margins down.

questions.q: A SWOT analysis would classify a new free-trade agreement opening up an export market as a:
options: Strength
Opportunity
Weakness
Threat
questions.explain: A favourable external development such as a new export market is an opportunity in SWOT.

questions.q: A monopoly market structure is characterised by:
options: Free and costless entry for all firms
Perfectly informed buyers and sellers
One dominant firm with significant market power
Many firms with no pricing power
questions.explain: A monopoly has a single dominant supplier with substantial control over price and market.

questions.q: A joint venture differs from a takeover because in a joint venture:
options: It is always between firms in unrelated industries
One firm gains full ownership and control of the other
No resources are ever pooled
Two or more firms set up and share a new, separate enterprise
questions.explain: In a joint venture, partner firms share ownership, risk and resources in a jointly created enterprise rather than one absorbing the other.

questions.q: A common cause of resistance to change among employees is:
options: Fear of the unknown and concern over job security
Excessive confidence that change will benefit them
An eagerness to lose established routines
A strong desire for more uncertainty
questions.explain: People often resist change because of fear of the unknown and worries about their jobs and status.

questions.q: In a decision tree, the value of a decision is the expected value of the chosen option minus:
options: The discount factor
The value of the rejected option
The initial cost of that option
The probability of success
questions.explain: Net expected value of an option = its total expected value minus the cost of undertaking it.

questions.q: A core competence, according to Hamel and Prahalad, is best described as:
options: A distinctive capability that is hard to imitate and gives access to many markets
Any activity the business performs, however ordinary
A short-term marketing campaign
The cheapest production process a firm uses
questions.explain: A core competence is a hard-to-imitate strength that provides competitive advantage and potential entry to multiple markets.
